strings.d1.s0.name: Odunpazarı Houses
strings.d1.s0.tips: Colourful Ottoman houses with bay windows and cobbled streets, quiet in the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Odunpazarı Modern Museum
strings.d1.s1.tips: Kengo Kuma's timber museum: contemporary Turkish art, with architecture that is an exhibit in itself.
strings.d1.s2.name: Çibörek Evi Odunpazarı
strings.d1.s2.tips: Tatar çibörek (fried meat pastry), served hot with ayran. Three or four will fill you up.
strings.d1.s3.name: Meerschaum Museum Eskişehir
strings.d1.s3.tips: Meerschaum carving in Odunpazarı, with a workshop and museum.
strings.d1.s4.name: Kurşunlu Complex
strings.d1.s4.tips: Odunpazarı's Ottoman complex, home to glass art workshops.
strings.d1.b0.name: Odunpazarı Met Helvası Shop
strings.d1.b1.name: Atlıhan Handicrafts Bazaar
strings.d2.s0.name: Porsuk River Gondola Tour
strings.d2.s0.tips: Take a gondola from Köprübaşı for a Venice feel, calm in the morning.
strings.d2.s1.name: Köprübaşı
strings.d2.s1.tips: The heart of the city, with bridges over the Porsuk and cafes.
strings.d2.s2.name: Haller Youth Centre
strings.d2.s2.tips: Cafes and art in the old market hall, with a student-town atmosphere.
strings.d2.s3.name: Mangal Keyfi Eskişehir
strings.d2.s3.tips: One of Eskişehir's best-known meat restaurants, famous for balaban köfte.
strings.d2.s4.name: Kent Park Eskişehir
strings.d2.s4.tips: An artificial beach and park on the Porsuk: sand beach in summer, walks in winter.
strings.d2.b0.name: Eskişehir Balaban Köfte Restaurant
strings.d2.b1.name: Eskişehir Contemporary Arts Gallery
strings.d2.b1.tips: A gallery in the centre, good for a rainy day.
strings.d3.s0.name: Sazova Science, Culture and Art Park
strings.d3.s0.tips: A fairytale castle, pirate ship and Japanese garden, good for a walk with or without children.
strings.d3.s1.name: Sabancı Space House
strings.d3.s2.name: Sazova Cafe
strings.d3.s3.name: Eti Underwater World
strings.d3.s4.name: Kentpark Waterfront Walk
strings.d3.s4.tips: An evening walk along the Porsuk.
strings.d3.b0.name: Sazova Çibörek Restaurant
strings.d3.b1.name: Air Museum Eskişehir
strings.d3.b1.tips: Aircraft museum, an alternative to the aquarium.
strings.d4.s0.name: Yazılıkaya Midas Monument
strings.d4.s0.tips: 80 km from Eskişehir: a Phrygian rock monument and the city of Midas, best in morning light.
strings.d4.s1.name: Phrygian Valley Rock Churches
strings.d4.s1.tips: Rock tombs and churches at Han, reached on foot.
strings.d4.s2.name: Han Village Restaurant
strings.d4.s2.tips: A village restaurant serving kuru fasulye (white bean stew) and gözleme (stuffed flatbread).
strings.d4.s3.name: Ayazini Village
strings.d4.s3.tips: Cappadocia-like fairy chimneys and a rock church, the loveliest village in the Phrygian Valley.
strings.d4.b0.name: Seyitgazi Complex Restaurant
strings.d4.b1.name: Seyitgazi Complex
strings.d4.b1.tips: The tomb of Battal Gazi and the complex, an alternative to Ayazini.
strings.d5.s0.name: Sivrihisar Grand Mosque
strings.d5.s0.tips: A Seljuk mosque with wooden columns, one hour from Eskişehir.
strings.d5.s1.name: Sivrihisar Armenian Church
strings.d5.s1.tips: A restored church, now a cultural centre.
strings.d5.s2.name: Sivrihisar Nasreddin Hoca House
strings.d5.s2.tips: Hoca's birthplace, the village of Hortu, is nearby. In town there is a memorial house.
strings.d5.s3.name: Sivrihisar Yemekçi
strings.d5.s3.tips: A town restaurant serving kuru fasulye (white bean stew) and rice pilaf.
strings.d5.s4.name: Pessinus Ancient City
strings.d5.s4.tips: A Cybele temple and theatre at Ballıhisar, in a Phrygian-Roman city.
strings.d5.b0.name: Sivrihisar Market Breakfast Place
strings.d5.b1.name: Nasreddin Hoca Hortu Village
strings.d5.b1.tips: Hoca's village, an alternative to Pessinus.
strings.d6.s0.name: Eskişehir Archaeology Museum
strings.d6.s0.tips: Finds from Dorylaion and the Phrygians.
strings.d6.s1.name: Glass Arts Museum
strings.d6.s1.tips: Glassblowing in Odunpazarı, with workshops to watch.
strings.d6.s2.name: Ciğerci Eskişehir
strings.d6.s2.tips: Eskişehir's liver wrap (ciğer dürüm), a student classic.
strings.d6.s3.name: Tepebaşı Art Street
strings.d6.s4.name: Vişnelik Garden Eskişehir
strings.d6.s4.tips: A city garden for a stroll.
strings.d6.b0.name: Eskişehir Historic Bulgur House
strings.d6.b1.name: Eskişehir Caricature Museum
strings.d6.b1.tips: Caricature art in Odunpazarı, an alternative to the glass museum.
strings.d7.s0.name: Odunpazarı Bazaar
strings.d7.s0.tips: Meerschaum, met helvası and glass souvenirs.
strings.d7.s1.name: Odunpazarı Breakfast Place
strings.d7.s1.tips: Breakfast, with met helvası for dessert.
strings.d7.s2.name: Eskişehir Railway Station
strings.d7.s2.tips: High-speed train: Ankara in 1.5 hours, Istanbul in 2.5 hours. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Odunpazarı Tatar Mantı House
strings.d7.b0.tips: Tatar mantı (small dumplings), a farewell meal.
strings.d7.b1.name: Porsuk River Walkway
strings.note0: The high-speed train (YHT) takes 2.5 hours from Istanbul and 1.5 hours from Ankara. The city tram (ESTRAM) goes everywhere in town. You will need a car for the Phrygian Valley and Sivrihisar.
strings.note1: Çibörek, balaban köfte, met helvası and Tatar mantı are local specialities, and Odunpazarı has plenty of çibörek places.
strings.note2: Winters are cold (-5°C) and snowy. Odunpazarı looks lovely under snow, and the museums are indoor options.
strings.note3: Odunpazarı Modern Museum is closed on Mondays. Entry is about 300 TL.
strings.note4: It is a student city: cafes are cheap and the evenings are lively.
strings.note5: Roads in the Phrygian Valley are dusty in summer, so set off early in the morning.
